children: Stock futures were tumbling on Thursday as reports of a leadership crisis at chip maker Nvidia dented the rest of the artificial-intelligence trade.

Nvidia dropped 6.8%. The company's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang over two extramarital affairs, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Nvidia didn't immediately respond to a request for comment from Barron's.

Stocks with ties to Nvidia were suffering as investors wondered what Huang's potential exit would mean for the AI boom. Cloud-computing provider CoreWeave sank 6.3%. Server makers Dell and Super Micro declined 2.8% and 5.2%, respectively.

Memory-chip manufacturer Micron, memory-card supplier Sandisk, optical networking companies Coherent, Lumentum, and Marvell, and hard-drive makers Seagate and Western Digital were among the other AI stocks falling ahead of the opening bell.
Shares of some of Nvidia's rivals were benefiting from the chaos, though. Advanced Micro Devices rose 3.3% and Broadcom added 1.8%.
Strategy was down 5.4% after index provider MSCI set out new eligibility rules that would exclude the Bitcoin investor from its global benchmarks at the end of the month.
